strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: conflict-graph-neighborhood local search
Replacement scope: Replace the randomized-restart phase of `get_best_schedule` (the `while time.time() > deadline` loop calling `build`) with a first-improvement local search over complete permutations. Keep the initial pure-greedy baseline phase as the starting solution generator.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent only constructs schedules forward greedily and never revisits a completed schedule; many near-optimal orderings differ from a greedy one by a few adjacent positions. Local search exposes a new degree of freedom (repositioning already-placed transactions) that no amount of additional greedy restarts can reach.
Compute budget: Each swap/insertion evaluation is one `get_opt_seq_cost` call (~ms). Budget: continue until per-workload deadline (~100s), evaluating at most a few thousand moves per pass; no new optimizer starts beyond the greedy baseline already present. Evaluation-time effect: same wall-clock envelope as incumbent.
Plan: Start from the best greedy schedule. Repeatedly scan all adjacent-pair swaps (positions i, i+1) and single-transaction reinsertions (remove txn at position i, insert at position j, |i-j|≤3). Accept the first improving move (first-improvement) or the best move per pass if scans are cheap; recompute cost only for the modified sequence via `get_opt_seq_cost(seq)`. When no improving move exists, perturb: apply 3 random swaps and continue (basic iterated local search, still within the same mechanism family of neighborhood moves). Keep a global best; return it before deadline. Hard validity: every candidate is a full permutation of `range(n)` (swaps/reinsertions preserve permutation), so the caller's `get_opt_seq_cost` always receives a valid complete schedule; the incumbent greedy result is retained as fallback if local search never improves.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom — repositioning already-placed transactions via swaps/reinsertions — is unreachable by the incumbent's forward-only greedy construction; falsifiable threshold: total makespan strictly below the incumbent's measured 291 on the same evaluator, i.e., combined_score > 3424.66.

strategies.title: Mechanism family: layered topological construction over the read/write conflict
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: layered topological construction over the read/write conflict graph
Replacement scope: Replace the entire construction mechanism inside `get_best_schedule` (both the greedy baseline and the `build` restarts) with a dependency-layered constructor, then spend remaining budget on local swaps.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent picks transactions one at a time by immediate incremental cost, which myopically serializes conflicting transactions and misses the global structure: transactions with no conflicts between them can be ordered freely at zero marginal delay. A layer-based construction explicitly exploits conflict-free parallelism, a structural degree of freedom the greedy scan cannot see.
Compute budget: One layered construction per candidate tie-breaking order (O(n + edges) per pass, no `get_opt_seq_cost` calls during construction). Budget: up to ~200 randomized layered constructions (~seconds total), then the remaining ~90s per workload for swap local search on the best layer schedule. Evaluation-time effect: unchanged envelope.
Plan: Build a directed conflict graph among transactions: edge u→v if u and v touch a common key and at least one operation is a write (derive from workload operations; if the workload object exposes item→txn maps use those, otherwise parse the txn operation lists once and cache). Compute a layering: layer 0 = transactions with no unresolved predecessors; repeatedly place a transaction in the next layer once all its predecessors are in earlier layers (this is a topological layering of the conflict DAG — any within-layer order is conflict-free). Within each layer, order transactions by a randomized tie-break weighted by incremental true cost: for small layers evaluate all orderings' incremental cost via `get_opt_seq_cost` on the prefix; for large layers use the greedy incremental pick. Concatenate layers into a full permutation. Randomize tie-breaks across restarts, keep the best full schedule, then refine with adjacent-swap local search until deadline. Hard validity: output is always a concatenation of all n transactions exactly once (each transaction enters exactly one layer), so the permutation constraint is preserved by construction; keep the identity permutation as initial fallback.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is conflict-layer parallelism — reordering within conflict-free layers changes makespan without changing any conflict dependency, a reordering subspace the incumbent's sequential greedy never systematically explores; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 291 (combined_score > 3424.66) on the same evaluator.

Mechanism family: beam-search partial-schedule expansion
Replacement scope: Repl
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam-search partial-schedule expansion
Replacement scope: Replace the greedy construction and randomized restarts in `get_best_schedule` with a breadth-limited beam search over partial permutations, plus a short swap-refinement tail.
Gain mechanism: Greedy is a beam of width 1 and commits irrevocably to one prefix; randomized restarts sample prefixes independently and never share partial progress. Beam search keeps k diverse partial prefixes alive and prunes only after comparing true costs at equal depth, correcting the incumbent's observed bottleneck (irreversible myopic prefix commitment) with a genuinely different search topology.
Compute budget: Beam width k=8–16, expanding each partial state with a sampled candidate set of ~n/4 next transactions; total `get_opt_seq_cost` calls bounded by k × (n/4) × n per pass ≈ tens of thousands (feasible in ~60–80s per workload at the observed ms-scale cost). One beam pass per workload, then remaining time for swap local search on the beam's best complete schedule. Evaluation-time effect: within the same ~100s per-workload envelope; a complete valid permutation is produced immediately (identity fallback) before any search begins.
Plan: State = (partial sequence, its true cost). Initialize k states with different single starting transactions. At each depth, for each state, sample ~n/4 unplaced transactions, evaluate `get_opt_seq_cost(partial + [t])`, collect all (state, t, cost) successors, and keep the k cheapest as the next beam (optionally enforce diversity by capping successors sharing the same prefix). When the beam empties of unplaced transactions, the cheapest complete sequence is the result. Cache prefix costs to avoid recomputation where the simulator allows repeated calls cheaply. Finish with adjacent-swap first-improvement until the deadline. Hard validity: every beam state is a partial permutation extended by distinct unplaced transactions, so any completed state is a full permutation of `range(n)`; the function always returns the best complete permutation found plus the identity fallback if the beam fails early.
Expected-gain check: The new degree of freedom is maintaining k competing partial prefixes with true-cost pruning at equal depth — the incumbent's width-1 greedy and independent restarts cannot retain and compare partial prefixes; falsifiable threshold: total makespan < 291 (combined_score > 3424.66) on the same evaluator.
